decisions.decision: A bare noun is grammatically number-neutral by default. It may denote one or more referents when context supplies the intended number. Nominal plural marking is optional and informative rather than obligatory.

Use the invariant pre-nominal particle wi as the optional explicit nominal plural marker. Canonical form /wi/; accepted accent-tolerant realization [u̯i] may be used where /w/ is not stable. Wi marks plurality only: it does not mark definiteness, gender, or agreement.

Normally omit wi when plurality or quantity is already explicit through a numeral or quantifier. Thus ter uman means three people and omni uman means all/every person or all people; redundant wi is not required.

Use invariant pre-nominal omni for universal quantification over members of a set: ALL / EVERY. It may receive collective or distributive interpretation from context. Examples: omni uman 'all people / every person'; tik omni uman 'all these people'; tan omni uman 'all those people'.

Use invariant pre-nominal tot for the total integrity or entirety of one referent or mass: WHOLE / ENTIRE. It is not the ordinary set-universal quantifier. Examples: tot dom 'the whole house'; tot dia 'the whole day'; tot mund 'the whole world'.
When a demonstrative and a quantifier co-occur, the demonstrative precedes the quantifier, which precedes the noun: tik omni uman; tes omni uman; tan omni uman.
Keep mi unassigned for now. It is reserved as a strong phonological form for a possible future grammatical function, but currently has no canonical meaning.

Use invariant pre-nominal nul for ZERO / NO quantity. It means that the set contains no referents: nul uman 'no person / nobody'; nul umano 'no man'; nul umane 'no woman'; nul dom 'no house'. Because nul already fixes quantity at zero, wi is not used with it.
Use invariant free si for YES and no for NO. The same free form no also serves as the pre-verbal sentential negator NOT; ka remains the separate polar-question marker.

Use hyphenated enclitic -si for additive focus ALSO / TOO (Italian anche / pure). It attaches to the right edge of the focused constituent: i-si 'I too'; tik uman-si 'this person too'. Free si 'YES' and bound -si are distinguished by syntax and orthography.

Use hyphenated enclitic -no for negative-additive focus NEITHER / NOT EVEN / NOT ... EITHER (Italian neanche / nemmeno). It attaches to the right edge of the focused constituent: i-no vidi 'not even I see'; dom-no 'not even the house'. Bound -no itself supplies clause-negative polarity for this ordinary reading, so an additional pre-verbal no is not required.

The focus enclitics -si and -no scope over the constituent whose right edge hosts them. In multiword nominal constituents the clitic is written on the final word: tik omni uman-si 'all these people too'; tik omni uman-no 'not even all these people'.

Use genitive -s by default and -es after stems ending in s, z, sj, tj, or dj. A stem ending in ts is covered by the final-s trigger. The support vowel preserves pronounceability for canonical sibilant edges and for sj/tj/dj when they surface coalescently as [sh]/[tsh]/[dzh]. Plain final j is the glide /j/ and does not by itself trigger -es.

Form personal possessives productively as genitives of the confirmed personal pronouns: i->is, u->us, a->as, in->ins, un->uns, an->ans. They are invariant and do not agree with the possessed noun. Optional third-person referential specificity remains inside the pronoun before genitive -s: ao->aos, ae->aes, ano->anos, ane->anes; neutral as/ans always remain valid.

Keep copula/existential root es. In the current person-number system its present explicit forms are esi, esu, esa, esin, esun, esan. Present-simple adjectival, nominal, and locative predicates may use zero copula; explicit es is available for emphasis/existence and supplies the verbal carrier when TAM is required. Copular TAM follows the canonical root + aspect + time + person + N order: simple past esdi/esdu/esda/esdin/esdun/esdan, simple future esfi/esfu/esfa/esfin/esfun/esfan, and aspectual examples esei/esoi, esedi/esodi, esefi/esofi.

Use invariant suffix -it productively on verbal roots to form the ordinary participial/resultative stem: dik->dikit 'detto', mov->movit 'mosso', vid->vidit 'visto', fak->fakit 'fatto/creato'. The /i/ is part of the suffix and avoids difficult root+t clusters. The syntax of compound tenses and passive constructions remains a separate decision.

Retire the legacy use of -it as an abstract quality/state suffix. Productive -it is reserved for participial/resultative forms; productive abstract qualities, states, and properties use confirmed -itat instead.

Use invariant suffix -itat productively to derive abstract qualities, states, and properties from suitable lexical bases. Canonical examples: bon->bonitat 'bonta', klar->klaritat 'chiarezza', uman->umanitat 'umanita'. The suffix is distinct from participial/resultative -it.

Every ordinary finite verb has the canonical morphotactic order root + aspect + time + person vowel + optional plural N. Person vowels are i (first), u (second), a (third); plural N follows the person vowel, yielding in, un, an. Aspect precedes time, and both precede person and number.

Keep invariant derivational suffix -ia for PLACE / INSTITUTION / FIELD / DOMAIN associated with a lexical base. Under current phonology it is canonically pronounced /i.a/ as hiatus, never /ja/ unless j is explicitly written. Examples are formed productively from current roots; legacy facia/docia are obsolete because their roots were replaced, not because -ia is invalid.

There are no obligatory articles. When explicit indefinite singularity is useful, reuse the cardinal numeral uno directly as the optional pre-nominal indefinite determiner: uno dom = 'one house / a house'. No separate apocopated article un is canonical; bare nouns remain valid when definiteness/singularity is contextually clear.

Use kom as the canonical WH-word HOW and ker as the canonical WH-word WHY. The earlier WHY form kur is retired. This keeps kom available for the question system because the Latin cum/com- lexical root is now kun, while the Latin cura lexical root is now kurar.
The finite time slot is closed to three values: zero for present, d for past, and f for future.

The finite aspect slot is closed to three values: zero simple, e ongoing/progressive, and o completed/perfect. Aspect precedes time, producing the 3×3 combinations by time rows: Ø/e/o, d/ed/od, f/ef/of. The former finite aspect markers n and b are retired.

Finite aspect e/o are grammar-critical vowels. In present aspect-marked forms they form canonical hiatus before the person vowel i/u/a (e.g. dikei = /dik.e.i/). Accentual raising or vowel coalescence is not permitted when it would erase the aspect contrast; aspect e/o must remain recoverably distinct from person i/u/a.

Ability, obligation, volition, learned capacity and related servile/modal meanings are expressed analytically by an ordinary finite servile verb followed by the bare infinitive/root of the lexical verb. The servile carries aspect, time, person and number; the dependent infinitive remains uninflected. Lexical roots for individual servile meanings are separate lexical decisions.
Retire the inherited synthetic m ability/potential marker from finite TAM. Modal/servile meanings are not a fourth aspect and are expressed through finite servile verb + bare infinitive instead.

A participial/resultative form in -it may be zero-nominalized and head a noun phrase without any additional nominalizer. In nominal use it denotes a result or resulting entity and follows ordinary noun grammar: bare fakit is number-neutral, wi fakit is explicitly plural, duo fakit is two facts/things done, and wi is omitted with numerals/quantity quantifiers. No special plural suffix is added to -it; ordinary nominal case marking remains available. Passive-clause syntax is a separate decision.

Close synthetic nominal case to six values: zero nominative/base, -em accusative, -s/-es genitive, -ad dative/allative, -de ablative, and -in locative. Synthetic case attaches to the head noun; modifiers remain invariant. Optional nominal plural wi is a separate pre-nominal particle.
Retire the inherited comitative suffix -ko. Express comitative WITH / TOGETHER WITH analytically as invariant pre-nominal kun + noun phrase, e.g. kun uman, kun tik uman, kun wi uman.

Retire -per, -pro, -due, -fin, -tem, and -mod as productive case suffixes. Preserve their meanings as invariant free pre-nominal relators: per instrumental/perlative, pro benefactive, due causal, fin purposive, tem temporal, mod manner. Canonical structure is RELATOR + NP, normally with the complement in base form.

Use invariant productive suffix -or for PERSON / AGENT: a person whose characteristic role or activity is to perform the action expressed by the canonical base. Historical agentive -er is retired. Parsing requires a valid canonical base; words that merely end in -or are not automatically segmented, so major and minor remain indivisible comparison words. Examples: fak->fakor maker/doer; dok->dokor teacher.

Use invariant productive suffix -il for TOOL / INSTRUMENT / DEVICE: an artifact, tool, machine, or device whose characteristic function is to perform, facilitate, or enable the action expressed by the canonical base. Historical instrumental -or is retired from this function. Examples: fak->fakil making tool/device; vid->vidil viewing/observation instrument. Syntactic means remains analytic with free relator per + NP.

Build the canonical state-phase family on es with fused prefixes and no hyphen: es = be/exist/hold state X; ines = remain/continue to be X; ades = become/enter state X; dees = cease to be/leave state X; rees = return to being X/become X again. dees does not imply becoming the lexical opposite. ades is used instead of aes because aes is already the canonical genitive/possessive of ae.

Canonize fused phase prefixes in-, ad-, de-, re- with invariant relations REMAIN/CONTINUE, ENTER/BEGIN, LEAVE/CEASE, RETURN/RESUME. They may combine compositionally with suitable verbal/predicative roots. With mov: inmov = continue moving, admov = begin moving, demov = cease moving, remov = resume moving. These prefixes are derivational/lexical phase operators and do not replace finite aspect Ø/e/o.

Canonize traes as the explicit two-pole state-transition verb. Canonical frame: traes DEST-ad SOURCE-de. The destination state/role takes existing dative/allative -ad and the source state/role takes existing ablative -de. Example: traes solidad likwidde = pass from liquid to solid; traes doktorad studentde = pass from student to doctor. This is distinct from ades X, which means simply become X and leaves the source state unspecified. No new transition case or relator is introduced.
